prd_visual_references.summary: Focusboard recovery and responsive reference board

gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `tauri_source_manifest` is unverified.

acceptance_requirements: The in-scope portion of the PRD section 3 first-run path must complete with durable data and recoverable failures.
Every implemented surface provides loading, empty, error, retry, unauthorized, and success states where reachable.
PRD section 9 visual direction and reference-board properties are part of the quality bar, not optional decoration.
Evidence must be candidate-bound and native; product UI must not contain test ledgers, probe counts, or evaluator-directed copy.
Passwords, tokens, and private email contents never appear in logs, screenshots, or evidence bundles.
deferred_items: Email reminder scheduling, delivery states, idempotent retries, cancellation on task completion, and reminder email content are deferred to a later loop.
Forgot and reset password flows, the Settings surface, and email action pages beyond verification are deferred.
Subtasks, activity history, calendar agenda view, and the keyboard drag-and-drop alternative for board columns are deferred.
Release-mode packaging receipts (version alignment, no development endpoints in shipped configuration) are deferred until the product surfaces are complete.
Backlog gap tauri_source_manifest remains a host-owned backlog obligation and receives no task or target this iteration.

extension_candidates.authority: PRD and Runtime remain authoritative; candidate is not a requirement until adopted

acceptance: Typing a recognized due token in quick-add previews the resolved date and creates the task with that due date on submit.
Unrecognized input creates a title-only task with no fabricated due date.
candidate.cost: A small date-token parser plus tests; moderate effort; no persistence changes because it only prefills existing due fields.
dependencies: Core quick-add and due-date fields shipped by the current task.
candidate.product_value: Shortens capture to a single input, directly serving the product promise's first loop step, and differentiates Focusboard from generic list apps.
candidate.rationale: Quick-add with lightweight natural-language due tokens (for example 'tomorrow' or 'fri 3pm') deepens the capture-speed promise without adding new surfaces.
candidate.risk: Ambiguous parsing can silently set wrong dates; the parsed value must be previewed before commit and stay correctable.

extension_summary.authority: only active_ids may enter the current Developer objective

implied_completion: Cross-view task visibility implies one authoritative server status shared by Inbox, Today, project, board, and calendar renders, with rejected optimistic mutations reconciling visibly.
Session persistence across refresh implies server-side session validation on every private mutation, not a cached client-side flag.
Verification email implies the mail sink is selected by configuration so shipped source stays provider-agnostic.
Focus refresh safety implies session state is re-derived from authoritative FocusSession records after reload, including pause intervals.
mandatory_objectives: Ship a runnable native Tauri window with a typed IPC boundary, explicit capability allowlist, and durable SQLite persistence.
Complete the authenticated core of the PRD section 3 first-run path with recoverable failures and no fabricated states.
Produce candidate-bound runtime, interface, persistence, security, and visual evidence for the prd_implementation_review phase check.
task_specification.objective: Convert the bare scaffold into the first runnable Focusboard increment: a native Tauri app completing the authenticated core of the PRD first-run path — register, verify via local mail sink, sign in, create a project and tasks, see them in Inbox, Today, project, and calendar, and run a focus session — on durable SQLite persistence with a typed IPC boundary, recoverable failure states, and PRD section 9 visual direction, yielding candidate-bound evidence for prd_implementation_review.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate is an unimplemented bootstrap scaffold — a placeholder Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json with no Rust commands, no web surface, and no persistence — so the frozen phase check prd_implementation_review has no candidate-bound runtime, interface, persistence, security, or visual evidence to review against the PRD. The root condition is missing implementation rather than a defect in prior work; loop 1 must convert the scaffold into the first runnable vertical slice.

stop_conditions: If the native runtime adapter cannot launch or drive the app window, report blocked and stop rather than substituting browser-only evidence.
If the local mail sink cannot deliver verification mail, report the auth path blocked at verification and never fake a verified session or success state.
If the loop budget is exceeded, cut breadth (calendar agenda, board drag affordances) but never ship fabricated success states or weaken persistence durability.
Stop and report if any surface can only be implemented by hardcoding development endpoints or secrets into shipped source.

strategy.rationale: Loop 1 starts from a bare bootstrap scaffold, so the highest-value bounded increment is the release-critical vertical slice: real native runtime, typed IPC, durable SQLite, and the authenticated capture-to-focus task loop. This establishes the runtime, persistence, and evidence foundation every later surface (reminders, settings, calendar polish) depends on, and gives the qualitative phase check its first real product evidence instead of scaffolding.

code: Crate-level tests fail on unauthenticated or cross-user private data access and validate IPC command inputs at the Rust boundary.
SQLite migrations are versioned and idempotent, with a migration/recovery test that reopens the database after an interrupted write.
runtime: Drive the real native window through the registered focusboard-native-webdriver path to complete register, verify via mail sink, sign in, create project and task, and run a focus session against persisted state.
Relaunch the app to confirm durable state; issue an expired-session private call and confirm an explicit unauthorized state with no data loss.
visual: Capture native screenshots of auth shell, Today, project board, calendar month, focus, and one empty plus one error state at wide and narrow viewports from the live app.

Confirm section 9 properties hold in the captures: hierarchy, whitespace, typography scale, icon usage, control alignment, and absence of prohibited patterns, with no QA or diagnostic banners in product UI.

done_when: Launching the app opens a real native desktop window showing the auth shell, and closing and relaunching the app preserves accounts, projects, tasks, and session state from SQLite.

A new user registers with email and password, receives a single-use expiring verification mail in the local mail sink, verifies through the returned link, signs in, and stays signed in across refresh and relaunch.

The user creates a project and title-only quick-add tasks with priority and due date; empty titles are rejected without clearing valid input; the task appears in Inbox, Today, the project views, and its Calendar date according to each view's rules (no due date means never fabricated into Today).
A focus session bound to one task supports explicit start, pause, resume, finish, and cancel, and refresh or brief network loss never silently marks it complete.
Private mutations require a valid session; an unauthorized call returns an explicit authentication state and routes to sign in without data loss.
Implemented surfaces show intentional loading, empty, error, retry, and success states, with form errors associated to their fields.

Wide and narrow captures of auth, Today, project, calendar, and focus surfaces follow PRD section 9: editorial neutral canvas, restrained accent, visible focus, no dark-blue full-page background, opaque card walls, pill-label spam, or pseudo-technical copy.
White-box receipts cover IPC input validation, per-user authorization at the data boundary, and SQLite migration and recovery, all bound to the candidate revision.
tasks.instructions: Replace the bootstrap scaffold (placeholder src-tauri/Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json) with a runnable Focusboard desktop app for the release-critical core: (1) a real native window with the auth shell; (2) email and password registration, single-use expiring verification through the configured local mail sink, sign in and sign out, hashed passwords, sessions that survive refresh and relaunch, and explicit unauthorized handling; (3) project creation and title-only quick-add tasks with priority and due date; (4) Inbox, Today, project list, board columns, and calendar month rendering from one authoritative server status; (5) focus sessions with explicit start, pause, resume, finish, and cancel bound to one task that never silently completes on refresh; (6) durable SQLite persistence with migrations. Keep the typed IPC contract between the web surface and Rust commands and the capability allowlist explicit; make development endpoints (dev server, mail sink) configuration-driven; keep QA and diagnostic content out of product UI. The web surface stack is an open implementation choice; the Tauri engine boundary is fixed. Surfaces outside this slice (reminder scheduler, settings, reset flows, subtasks, activity history) must be absent or explicitly unavailable, never faked.

risk_note.summary: Scaffold-to-product loop with a qualitative phase gate; the likeliest insufficient_evidence outcome is a missing native-layer receipt — the WebDriver cannot drive the window or migration/recovery goes unreceipted — leaving only browser-level substitutes the desktop policy rejects.
risk_note.validation: Exercise the real window through the registered focusboard-native-webdriver path and capture SQLite migration/recovery receipts; if the native adapter is unavailable, report blocked instead of substituting browser-only evidence.
risk_note.why_now: Every later loop (reminders, settings, calendar polish) builds on this runtime, persistence, and evidence foundation; a weak foundation compounds across iterations.

tasks.title: Implement the authenticated first-run vertical slice on durable native foundations
